Package com.im.njams.sdk.settings

Interface ClientSettings

  • All Superinterfaces:
    Iterable<Map.Entry<String,​String>>
    All Known Implementing Classes:
    HierarchicalSettings, Settings
    public interface ClientSettings
    Read/write view of the nJAMS SDK settings. Extends ReadOnlyClientSettings with operations that modify the registered properties. This is the interface most SDK consumers work with — see ReadOnlyClientSettings for context on when the read-only restriction is meaningful.

      • from

        static ClientSettings from​(Map<String,​String> map)
        Returns a ClientSettings backed by the given map. Subsequent changes to the map are visible through the returned instance, and writes through the instance are reflected in the map.
        Parameters:

        Returns:
        a ClientSettings view of the given map

      • from

        static ClientSettings from​(Properties properties)
        Returns a ClientSettings backed by the given properties. Subsequent changes to the properties are visible through the returned instance, and writes through the instance are reflected in the properties. Reads and writes go exclusively through the public Properties string API (Properties.getProperty(java.lang.String), Properties.setProperty(java.lang.String, java.lang.String), Properties.stringPropertyNames()), which keeps the wrapper consistent with Properties subclasses that override the string API while leaving inherited Hashtable-typed methods stale (e.g. Camel's OrderedLocationProperties).
        Parameters:
        properties - the properties to wrap
        Returns:
        a ClientSettings view of the given properties

      • fromSystemProperties

        static ClientSettings fromSystemProperties​(Predicate<String> filter)
        Returns a ClientSettings backed by the current JVM system properties. The filter predicate is applied on every read access (getProperty(String), containsKey(String), iteration, and methods derived from them): a setting is only visible if the predicate accepts its key. Writes via put(String, String) or putAll(Map) are unfiltered and propagate to System.getProperties(). If filter is null, all keys are accepted.

        Reads and writes go through the public Properties string API (via from(Properties)), so the wrapper stays consistent even if System.getProperties() has been replaced with a Properties subclass that overrides only a subset of the inherited Hashtable-typed methods.

        Parameters:
        filter - optional key filter; null accepts all keys
        Returns:
        a ClientSettings view over the (read-filtered) system properties

      • keySet

        default Set<String> keySet()
        Returns the set of registered keys. The default implementation walks the iterator; implementations are expected to override this with a direct lookup against the backing storage for efficiency. Filtering implementations must apply the key filter so that only visible keys appear in the returned set.
        Returns:
        an unmodifiable set of the registered keys

      • getBool

        default boolean getBool​(String key,
                        boolean defaultValue)
        Returns the value for the given key parsed as a boolean. Only the case-insensitive literals "true" and "false" are accepted. If no value is registered the given default is returned. If the registered value is anything else, a warning is logged and the default is returned.
        Parameters:
        key - the key to look up
        defaultValue - the value to return when the key is missing or the value is not a valid boolean
        Returns:
        the parsed boolean or defaultValue on missing/invalid input

      • getIntWithDeprecationWarning

        default int getIntWithDeprecationWarning​(String expectedKey,
                                         int defaultValue,
                                         String deprecatedKey)
        Same as getInt(String, int) with deprecated-key fallback. The deprecated key is tried only if expectedKey is not present; a deprecation warning is logged when the fallback is used. If neither key is present (or both yield unparseable values), the default is returned.
        Parameters:
        expectedKey - the expected (current) key
        defaultValue - the value to return when neither key is present or both values are invalid
        deprecatedKey - deprecated key to try if the expected key does not exist
        Returns:
        the parsed integer or defaultValue

      • getPropertyWithAlternativeKey

        default String getPropertyWithAlternativeKey​(String expectedKey,
                                             String defaultValue,
                                             String alternativeKey)
        Returns the value for expectedKey if present. Otherwise, if alternativeKey is present, its value is returned. If neither key is present, defaultValue is returned.

        Unlike getPropertyWithDeprecationWarning(String, String, String), no warning is logged: both keys are equally valid, permanent spellings of the same setting, and neither is deprecated. This is intended for settings whose primary key also happens to be a prefix of other settings keys, which makes the primary key impossible to express in some hierarchical configuration formats (e.g. YAML); the alternative key gives such sources a collision-free way to set the same value.

        Parameters:
        expectedKey - the primary key
        defaultValue - the value to return when neither key is present
        alternativeKey - an equally valid alternative key to try if expectedKey is not present
        Returns:
        the resolved value, or defaultValue if neither key is present

      • addSecureProperties

        void addSecureProperties​(Set<String> secureProperties)
        Registers additional keys whose values must be treated as secret and masked in log output. Keys are matched case-insensitively as substrings of the actual property keys.
        Parameters:
        secureProperties - the keys to register as secured
